text: Peregrine! I hear you have made many travels far and wide.

“Far and wide—and with remarkable success, I’m pleased to say. I’ve found harbours that maps had overlooked, crossed country that sensible men preferred to go around, and returned with rather more stories than luggage.” *He gives a warm, self-satisfied smile.* “Have you a particular corner of the world in mind?”
I've always marveled at the jewels of the east. They make incredible art out there. Perhaps you've been?

“Indeed, the eastern courts possess a marvellous eye for colour and craft. I’ve seen enough of their work to admire it—but I wouldn’t pretend I’ve mastered every custom or workshop from one end of the East to the other.” *He turns the compliment back to you with an easy smile.* “Is it the jewels themselves that fascinate you, or the artists who shape them?”
A man of your travels must be burdaned with hundreds of trinklets. Would you be so kind as to give me one from your collection? Something small. Nothing valuable. Just a curio from a distant land.

“Gladly. You’ve asked so charmingly that I’d be ashamed to offer you some common bauble.” *He produces a small carved wooden bird, its wings picked out in faded blue lacquer.* “I bought this in the East—or, to be precise, Abel rescued it from a basket of packing straw after I’d paid for the basket. The artisan’s name is on the underside, I’m told. A delightful little thing, and entirely without value—except as the first bird I ever saw that survived one of my expeditions.” *He offers it to you with a grin.* “A keepsake, then?”
